A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FlexMerge study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison; relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v2 reports original vision, language, multimodal, OOD, ablation, and runtime results in Section 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds WUDI-Merging evaluations and further merging-time measurements.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Equation (1) retain the same greedy, minimum-cosine group-merging rule. However, v3 newly describes using SLINK/single linkage, which does not match that rule. The PDFs do not resolve whether this is an erroneous implementation description or a different merging procedure. WUDI is otherwise applied directly within the existing framework.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 8/30-task vision benchmarks, 11-task PEFT benchmark, 7-task full-fine-tuning benchmark, four multimodal tasks, and six OOD evaluation tasks. The additions reuse existing task coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds WUDI-Merging to the vision comparisons in Appendix C.1, Figures 8–9, alongside the retained Averaging, PCB-Merging, and TSV-M results. The other comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Table 2 extends the merging-time experiment from ViT-B/32 to include ViT-L/14. The new WUDI experiments use a learning rate of 10^-5 and 300/1000 iterations for 8/30 tasks. Previously reported dataset processing, metrics, training settings, and inference-batch procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 2 extends the efficiency analysis to test merging costs with the larger ViT-L/14 model. The similarity-function and merging-order ablations, random-selection comparisons, OOD tests, reconstruction-latency analysis, and other appendix analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The uncertainty reporting in Table 3 and existing variability displays are unchanged. v3 adds no repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: Figures 8–9 add WUDI accuracy-size curves for both vision encoders. Table 2 retains the ViT-B/32 timings and adds ViT-L/14 timings: approximately 3.4/31 seconds for FlexMerge and 2.6/6.1 seconds for TA on 8/30 tasks. Existing accuracy curves and other numerical tables are retained.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 adds a substantive three-stage complexity derivation, covering similarity computation, merge ordering, and parameter merging, and concluding O(BM^2 d_max). v2 offered only qualitative efficiency discussion. The new derivation's identification of Equation (1) with single linkage is inconsistent with its minimum cross-group cosine rule.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims: flexible data-free merging across sizes, steep initial accuracy gains, changing algorithm rankings, and negligible inference overhead. The additional experiments support the existing contribution scope.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 adds an explanation that increased model size reduces parameter interference, diminishing the extra benefit of mechanisms such as TIES trimming and PCB competition balancing. The existing architectural and theoretical limitations in Section 5 remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-availability statement and repository link, WUDI implementation settings in Appendix B.1, and details about precomputed merge orders, SLINK, heap merging, and deferred parameter merging. The hardware and compute-resource disclosures in Appendix D remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds WUDI-Merging (Cheng et al., 2025), including its classification in Table 4, and references Sibson's SLINK algorithm and Knuth for the complexity discussion. The broader positioning against existing merging approaches is retained.

P1.justification: v3 adds limited explanatory passages, acknowledgments, and an LLM-usage appendix, alongside author-contact, conference-header, and terminology edits. The main narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Algorithm 1 changes from a compact display beside prose to a full-width display, and Table 1 is enlarged and relocated. Figures 8–9 gain fourth panels, Table 2 gains a model column, and Table 4 gains a WUDI row. Remaining figures retain their content despite page reflow.

improvement.justification: The WUDI comparisons, larger-model timings, and code-access information provide useful incremental gains. However, the new complexity analysis invokes SLINK/single linkage while the retained minimum-cosine rule corresponds to complete linkage, leaving the implementation description and runtime argument unreconciled. These benefits coexist with an unresolved issue concerning the central merging procedure, so the PDFs do not support a reliable net quality judgment.
